verdict: Decent overall; 2017 is the first-year 1.5T with a known cold-weather oil-dilution issue (fuel in oil). Low miles (87k) helps, but history unknown.
major_issues: Oil dilution (gas in oil), mostly cold climates, TSB/software + warranty extension 2018; A/C compressor/condenser failures (~60-100k, $800-1,400); CVT generally OK but fluid service matters; catalytic converter failure linked to dilution ($1,500+); infotainment glitches.
risk_reason: 87k mi is low for this lot; most issues are warranty-extended or occur earlier. Main risk is A/C or dilution-related damage if oil never changed.
inspect_today: Check dipstick for gasoline smell and level above full mark; oil cap/oil colour; A/C blows cold and compressor clutch engages; CVT test drive for shudder; scan for codes; check NHTSA recalls by VIN and whether Honda software update done; cold-start rattle.

verdict: One of the most dependable compact SUVs; K24 engine with CVT (2015-16) is durable past 200k with maintenance.
major_issues: Early 2015-16 CVT judder/software fixes; A/C compressor/condenser (~80-120k, $800-1,400); engine mount vibration; rear differential/AWD fluid neglect; brake wear; oil consumption rare.
risk_reason: 127k mi is mid-life for the K24; typical needs are maintenance (brakes, fluids) under $1,000. A/C is the most likely larger bill.
inspect_today: CVT smoothness from stop and at 30-45 mph, no shudder; A/C cold; AWD rear diff fluid condition if accessible; engine mounts vibration at idle; coolant and oil condition; suspension noises; scan codes.

verdict: Simple Nu 1.8 + 6-speed auto; solid, cheap to fix, though 140k with unknown history is a gamble. Not part of the big Theta II engine failures.
major_issues: Some oil consumption on Nu engines at high miles; transmission shift flare if fluid neglected; AC condenser/blower resistor; wheel bearings, suspension bushings; steering column noise (flex joint ~$300-600).
risk_reason: 140k, as-is; parts cheap, but a worn transmission or oil burning would exceed $1,000. Typical wear items stay under budget.
inspect_today: Dipstick level and colour (low oil = consumption); exhaust smoke on cold start; transmission shift quality, no flare/slip; steering column clunk; suspension noises; AC; scan codes; recall check.

verdict: 2020 Elantra 2.0 Nu MPI with IVT; Hyundai recall for piston-ring heat treatment (2019-2020 Elantra, 21V-301 area). 176k miles is extremely high for a 2020 (heavy use, likely rideshare/fleet).
major_issues: Piston oil ring defect: oil consumption, cylinder scuffing, engine failure; IVT (CVT) judder/whine; AC compressor; electrical/infotainment issues. Engine replacement $4,000-7,000 if out of coverage; Hyundai powertrain warranty is 10yr/100k to original owner only, 5/60 for subsequent.
risk_reason: Very high mileage for age (likely fleet/rideshare), outside warranty, with a documented engine ring defect and IVT concerns; any major failure is far over budget.
inspect_today: Check oil level/condition and whether the oil is very low; blue smoke; listen for ticking/knock; compression-related misfire codes; IVT whine/judder; check VIN for recall completion and any engine replacement; service records; reject if oil is low or sludgy.

verdict: 2018 Kona SE 2.0 Nu MPI with 6-speed automatic (not the problematic DCT). Average; ring defect recall mainly 2019-2021, but oil consumption reports exist. 159k is high.
major_issues: Oil consumption on Nu 2.0 at high miles; engine failure reports; wheel-speed/ABS sensor and electrical glitches; AC; suspension components; some transmission shift complaints.
risk_reason: 159k out of warranty on a young model; many wear items due, and oil consumption could signal engine trouble. Likely under $1,000 only if engine is healthy.
inspect_today: Dipstick oil level and colour; smoke on startup/acceleration; engine noise; transmission shift smoothness; AC; suspension clunks (struts, links); battery/electrical warnings; recall status for VIN.

verdict: 2.4L GDI Theta II has a notorious record of bearing wear/engine seizure and fire recalls; 2017 is a later build with fixes, but 170k miles is risky for an as-is buy.
major_issues: Theta II engine failure/seizure (rod bearings, 60-150k) $4,000-7,000; excessive oil consumption; engine fires (EA21003 investigation, KSDS software); knock sensor detection recall; AC; wheel bearings; turbo not applicable. Lifetime engine warranty only for the original owner under settlement.
risk_reason: 170k, AWD, known engine-failure design; an as-is auction car likely lacks transferable coverage. A single failure blows the budget.
inspect_today: Check dipstick (low oil, metal flakes, burnt smell); listen for rod knock or ticking at cold start; look for KSDS update sticker/recall completion by VIN; check for engine replacement history; oil leaks; blue smoke; AWD clutch/diff noises; transmission shifts.

verdict: 3.3L Lambda II V6 with 6-speed is a sturdier powertrain than the 2.4 Theta; average reliability, adequate at 147k with maintenance. Some 3.3 V6 engine bearing recalls exist for other Hyundais.
major_issues: Crankshaft position sensor and oil pressure sensor leaks; AWD/ABS electrical; some engine seizures reported (~107k); timing belt/chain-related; water pump/coolant leaks; brake and suspension wear on a heavy 3-row.
risk_reason: Sturdy V6 but at 147k with bigger-ticket parts (AWD, suspension on a heavy vehicle); moderate chance of a >$1,000 bill, mostly from wear items or leaks.
inspect_today: Check oil level and for leaks at oil sensor/valve covers; coolant leaks at water pump; transmission shift quality; AWD behaviour; suspension bushings and control arms; brakes; ABS/airbag lights; scan for codes; verify recall completion.

verdict: 2015 Sonata Hybrid with 2.4L Theta II engine and 6-speed hybrid auto at 188k: worst of this batch. Combines engine-failure risk, aging hybrid battery and a complex drivetrain.
major_issues: Hybrid battery degradation/failure ($3,000-8,000); catastrophic hybrid system failure (~130k, ~$5,300); 2.4 GDI engine bearing/seizure; transmission/clutch problems (~110k, $5,000); engine stalling; 4 recalls; oil consumption.
risk_reason: 188k miles, out of hybrid battery warranty, complex hybrid system plus Theta II engine; failure of any major component is over budget and likely uneconomic to repair.
inspect_today: Scan hybrid system with OBD tool for battery state/codes and warnings; check hybrid/engine lights; listen for rod knock; engine oil level and condition; test drive for transmission clunk, hesitation, EV-to-engine transitions; A/C cooling of battery pack (fan noise); check recall completion; likely skip.
